summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with type II diabetes, was admitted due to severe hyperglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis after missing six days of evening insulin. She was treated with an IV insulin drip and fluids, which resolved her DKA. During the hospitalization, large abscesses on her inner thighs were discovered and surgically drained. Cultures grew Group B Streptococcus and methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus, and she was transitioned from broad-spectrum IV antibiotics to oral Augmentin. Her insulin regimen was adjusted to better control glucose, and metformin was discontinued. She improved clinically, with stable vitals and no further fevers, and was discharged home with wound care support, a 10-day antibiotic course, and follow-up appointments.
problems: Diabetes with ketoacidosis, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
